newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Shots fired at Serb car on Bosnia boundary road.
newsitem.headline: Shots fired at Serb car on Bosnia boundary road.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb civilian car came under gunfire while travelling on a road skirting Bosnian government territory near Sarajevo on Friday and a 60- year-old woman was wounded, the United Nations said.

Bosnian government police detained two Serb men in the targeted car for reasons that were not immediately clear, stoking tensions on the Serb side of the ethnic boundary line south of Sarajevo, a U.N. spokesman said.

Violence along the so-called Inter-Entity Boundary Line in Bosnia, which divides the Serb republic from the Moslem-Croat federation, has increased in the approach to Bosnia's first postwar elections on September 14.

Alex Ivanko, spokesman for the International Police Task Force (IPTF) in postwar Bosnia, said a woman in the car was hit four times by bullets in the 8.30 a.m. (0630 GMT) ambush near Trnovo 30 km (18 miles) south of Sarajevo. She was taken to a nearby hospital.
The road from Sarajevo to Trnovo crosses alternating strips of Bosnian government and separatist Serb terrain. The location of the shooting suggested it occurred in government territory.
"Two Serb men among the five occupants of the car were detained by (Bosnian) federation police in the area where the incident occurred," Ivanko told Reuters.
The police chief in the Serb-controlled town of Kula between Trnovo and Sarajevo demanded the immediate release of the two Serbs, hinting at reprisals if they were not.
"The police chief advised us the Serbs are quite tense and want the two freed immediately," said Ivanko.
The identity of the assailants and their motive were not immediately known.
A white civilian car with five men inside was reported in the vicinity of the targeted Serb vehicle but its connection with the attack was unclear.
IPTF monitors on the scene told Reuters earlier that one of the detained Serbs was a Trnovo policeman.
